result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [list_adapters()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: List the formats available for contract import and export. twitter-card: title: >- [list_adapters()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: List the formats available for contract import and export. title: >- [list_adapters()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: List the formats available for contract import and export. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} List the formats available for contract import and export. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/adapters/_registry.py#L182-L256){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature list_adapters() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Every format that [`import_contract()`](`pointblank.import_contract`) and [`export_contract()`](`pointblank.export_contract`) can work with is provided by a registered adapter. `list_adapters()` reports what's registered in the current session: the four built-in formats plus any custom adapters added with [`register_adapter()`](`pointblank.register_adapter`). It's useful for finding the right value for `format=`, for checking whether a format supports import, export, or both before calling either function, and for seeing which file extensions are used to detect a format. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, dict]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary, sorted by format name, that maps each format name to a dictionary with these keys: - `"class"`: the name of the adapter class - `"file_extensions"`: the list of file extensions used to detect the format - `"supports_import"`: whether the format can be imported with `import_contract()` - `"supports_export"`: whether the format can be exported with `export_contract()` ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} With no custom adapters registered, the result lists the four built-in formats. ::: {#12c69bbe .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb adapters = pb.list_adapters() list(adapters) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['dbt', 'frictionless', 'json_schema', 'odcs'] ``` ::: ::: Each entry describes one adapter. Here's the entry for the dbt adapter, which claims the `.yml` and `.yaml` file extensions and supports both directions. ::: {#2622e776 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} adapters["dbt"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'class': 'DbtAdapter', 'file_extensions': ['.yml', '.yaml'], 'supports_import': True, 'supports_export': True} ``` ::: ::: Since the result is an ordinary dictionary, it's easy to filter. This finds the formats that a contract can be exported to. ::: {#680d71c0 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} [name for name, info in adapters.items() if info["supports_export"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['dbt', 'frictionless', 'json_schema', 'odcs'] ``` ::: ::: All four built-in formats support export, so the list is the same as before. An adapter added with [`register_adapter()`](`pointblank.register_adapter`) may be import-only, though, so a check like this is useful before calling [`export_contract()`](`pointblank.export_contract`) with a format chosen at run time. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~register_adapter`) : Add a custom format to this list. [](`~pointblank.import_contract`) : Import a definition in one of the listed formats. [](`~pointblank.export_contract`) : Export a contract to one of the listed formats.
